title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling policies will cover legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files
summary: Hold: the location-control path stops before the documented location settings, and the briefing incorrectly treats the general encryption prerequisites as unconfirmed for legacy files. It also says existing policies have covered only Open XML files even though its cited documentation supports PDFs.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans service-side evaluation and sensitivity labeling of Word .doc, Excel .xls and PowerPoint .ppt files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview server-side auto-labeling will support legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt). Organizations can automatically evaluate and apply sensitivity labels to these files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Labels applying encryption through an auto-labeling policy that includes SharePoint or OneDrive must use Assign permissions now.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Labels applying encryption through an auto-labeling policy that includes SharePoint or OneDrive must set User access to content expires to Never.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: encryption prerequisites
claims.claim: Whether the SharePoint and OneDrive encryption prerequisites apply to legacy formats is not stated.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.
claims.fix: Remove 'Whether legacy formats are handled the same way is not stated.' and the encryption-prerequisites Open questions bullet. The documented prerequisite is scoped to policies including SharePoint or OneDrive locations, which includes this change; it is not restricted to particular file extensions.
